claims.text: The driver's own trace measures the continuous in-geofence dwell at 179 seconds — a single run of 19 consecutive fixes from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36 — against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180, which is the figure POL-NS-01(c) directs be read from the record rather than from fee_schedule.defaults). POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous dwell of at least that free waiting period. 179 seconds does not meet 180, so limb (c) fails by one second. POL-NS-06 then governs: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

Independently of limb (c), limb (d) of POL-NS-01 also fails. For limb (d) the trip must be terminated at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and the dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix — 22:38:37 — not from the driver's arrival tap. 180 seconds from 22:38:37 elapses at 22:41:37, but the trip was terminated at 22:41:36, one second early. The driver's own statement that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is therefore contradicted by his own trace, which records a 1-second shortfall. Because limbs (c) and (d) both fail, the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the refund falls to be made under POL-NS-06.

The driver cannot bridge the one-second gap by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, with geometry covering the pickup road and an active window covering the waiting period, carries a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING — the artifact carries no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own record states that no advisory covers Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 in this window. A MISSING advisory makes limb (i) unavailable, so it cannot be asserted to excuse or extend the shortfall. In any event the trace shows only a single in-geofence interval (accumulated_dwell.run_count = 1), so there is no second interval for limb (i) to add to the first. The 179-second shortfall therefore stands unmodified.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it'. Here POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full — limbs (c) and (d) each fail on the 179-second dwell — and POL-NS-06 positively displaces the charge. The driver therefore has no payout under POL-NS-07, and the $4.50 cancellation fee is not a sum that has been earned and retained by him; it is a charge that should never have been levied.

The amount the rider contests is exactly the cancellation-fee line on the ledger: the fare_breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the rider filed this dispute. Refunding that line in full under POL-NS-06 returns the whole contested amount to the filing party, which is FULL_REFUND as POL-GEN-03 defines it. The rider's claim is that the $4.50 should not have been charged at all, and on the 179-second dwell that claim is entirely right.

The evidence carrying the deciding fact is clean and unimpaired, so the confidence cap on the governing artifacts does not fall below the platform-wide escalation floor and no escalation is required. Both the gps_trace (EV-GPS-02717) and the trip_record (EV-TRIP-02717) are rated COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes: 100.0% coverage, 10-second cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and 19 qualifying in-geofence fixes across the measured run, all well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (min_distance_m 0.31 m). The arrival marker at 22:38:37 is not a false marker — the first qualifying in-geofence fix falls at the same timestamp — so POL-NS-05 does not fire and nothing in the record casts doubt on the 179-second measurement. The shortfall is arithmetic on admissible evidence and the rider is entitled to a monetary ruling rather than a referral.

claims.text: The driver's own trace proves arrival under POL-NS-02: 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, running continuously from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, with his closest fix 0.31 m from the pickup pin. POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied on the platform's own measurement, not on the driver's say-so.

The arrival marker was true, so POL-NS-05 does not fire and the waiting clock is not recomputed: at the 22:38:37 'I'm Here' tap the trace places the driver stationary at 0.0 km/h essentially on the pin (0.31 m), far inside both the 50 m arrival radius and the 300 m POL-NS-05 leash. There is no false-arrival finding to make against him.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on its face: the trip was terminated by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises, and no boarding event is recorded anywhere in the trip record.

The fee line carries no integrity defect: the fare ledger's cancellation_fee of 4.50 SGD reconciles exactly with the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50 in force for this trip, so POL-NS-08(d) has nothing to bite on and there is no basis in the record to disturb the amount charged.

The evidence is clean and this case is decidable: the GPS export is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage, 74 fixes, a maximum sampling gap of 0.0 s and both driver and rider tracks present, and the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count, so no limb of POL-NS-08 fires, nothing caps confidence below the floor and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is presented by this record.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log contains exactly one message in total, sent by the driver ('im at the pickup point', 22:38:57, read 22:39:27). The rider sent nothing at all.

On the rider's own device track the rider never approached the pickup: 53 rider fixes all sit between 895 m and 903 m from the pin, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed and not merely undecidable.

The rider's account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the platform's own telemetry: accepted 22:30:19, navigating from 22:30:27, arrival tapped 22:38:37 after 8.3 minutes en route, cancellation at 22:41:36 — the counterparty statement ('I waited the free period then cancelled') is what the event chain actually shows.

Nothing in the driver's profile bars compensation under POL-NS-07: no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4-termination limb, and against completed_trips_30d of 91 that is a rate of 0.022, below the 0.08 limb. Both limbs of the anti-farming check are required and neither trips; no other profile field may be read into that test.

On a fee that stands under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force — the money block computes 3.60 SGD against the 4.50 SGD fee — and the emitted outcome is a driver payment, not a bare declination.

The in-geofence dwell measured by the export is 179 seconds, one second short of the 180-second free waiting period, and the driver does not dispute that figure; but at every fix from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36 the driver was stationary on the pin and his trace runs on to 22:42:46 without him leaving, so the single-second difference is a boundary effect of a 10-second-cadence export rather than an early abandonment. There is in any event no second in-geofence interval for POL-NS-06(i) to add (run_count 1), and advisory EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the driver's case does not rest on that limb.

The contested amount is the cancellation fee actually charged and still standing — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, total_charged 4.50 — so on this rider-filed dispute a NO_ACTION outcome preserves the present payment state and the driver keeps the fee, unless some clause affirmatively displaces POL-NS-01.

ruling.explanation: The charge turns on one number: how long the driver held the pickup. Both parties agree the driver reached the pin and tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37, and that he terminated the trip at 22:41:36. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the arrival tap. The free period in force is read from the record: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds. The platform's own GPS trace measures a single continuous in-geofence run of 179 seconds (19 qualifying fixes, 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, closest fix 0.31 m from the pin). That is one second short of 180. POL-NS-01 limb (c) therefore fails, and limb (d) fails with it: 180 seconds from 22:38:37 elapses at 22:41:37, and the driver cancelled at 22:41:36. Because the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-06 governs - where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. To the driver: your point that the arrival marker was true, that you were stationary on the pin the whole time and that the trace runs on to 22:42:46, is accepted - POL-NS-02 is satisfied (19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius) and POL-NS-05 does not fire (0.0 km/h at the pin at 22:38:37). But POL-NS-02 decides arrival, not dwell. Your argument that the one-second gap is a boundary effect of the 10-second export cadence is understood and is factually plausible, but POL-NS-06 is deliberately strict liability - the policy states that even a rider who was genuinely absent gets the fee back where the driver cancelled a few seconds early - and there is no de minimis allowance anywhere in the category. The shortfall also cannot be bridged: POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only against a present, populated traffic_advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), while the trace shows a single interval (run_count 1). POL-NS-07 accordingly pays you nothing: it applies only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it', and here POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-06 displaces it, so the 3.60 SGD payout is not owed; nor does the anti-farming check arise (no_show_terminations_30d 2, below the 4-limb, rate 0.022, below 0.08). To the rider: your account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not what the record shows - he was en route 8.3 minutes and waited 2 minutes 59 seconds - and POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you (you sent no message, and your device track sits about 900 m from the pin). You succeed on the dwell arithmetic alone, which POL-NS-06 makes decisive regardless of rider presence. Integrity: the fare ledger's cancellation-fee line of 4.50 reconciles exactly with the platform fee of 4.50, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect; the trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage and no gaps, and the chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count, so no POL-NS-08 limb fires and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is presented. The ruling rests on EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, both at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The refund of 4.50 SGD is at or below the 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically. No clause produces a referral.

To the rider and the driver — this decision concerns the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02717 (EV-FARE-02717: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

THE DRIVER DID ARRIVE, BUT THE WAITING PERIOD WAS NOT SERVED. The GPS export (EV-GPS-02717) places 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes on the pin (closest 0.31 m) inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the 'I'm Here' tap at 22:38:37 is a true marker, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied, POL-NS-05 does not fire, and POL-NS-01 limb (b) holds. I accept the driver's account that he waited, and I reject the rider's description of a cancellation 'almost immediately' — the record shows 8.3 minutes en route (EV-TRIP-02717). But the fee turns on more than arrival.

POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force — 180 seconds, read from the record's own platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02717) — measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 22:38:37, not from the arrival tap. The platform's own export measures that continuous dwell at 179 seconds (longest qualifying run, 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, 19 fixes), one second short of 180. The trip was terminated at 22:41:36, one second before the required dwell would have elapsed at 22:41:37, so POL-NS-01 limb (d) also fails.

The driver's two answers to this do not hold. First, the 'boundary effect of a 10-second cadence' argument: POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability — the waiting period is the consideration the fee buys — and the shortfall appears on both clocks (the export's 179 s dwell, and the platform's own wait timer started 22:38:39 and cancelled 22:41:36, i.e. 177 s). Second, the suggestion that the time be topped up: POL-NS-06(i) allows separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only against a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); in any event the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is nothing to add.

THE OUTCOME. On a dwell shorter than the free waiting period, POL-NS-06 is the governing clause: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full — 4.50 SGD — whether or not the rider was present. No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not; POL-NS-06 displaces the charge, so the 3.60 SGD payout the driver asks for is not earned. His anti-farming position (no_show_terminations_30d 2, a rate of 0.022 against 91 completed trips in 30 days) is accepted but never reached, because the fee itself was not earned.

CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. The evidence is clean: the GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (100 percent coverage, 74 fixes, maximum gap 0.0 s, both tracks present), the chat log reconciles to chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles to the fee in force — so no POL-NS-08 limb (a) to (d) fires, no artifact carrying the deciding fact is impaired below 1.0, and confidence (0.90) sits above the 0.70 floor. This is not a POL-NS-09 escalation. The monetary effect (4.50 SGD) is below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund executes automatically on issue.

REFERRALS. None. The arrival marker was true, so no POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record arises; the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one POL-NS-01 limb (d) expressly recognises, so there is no mis-selected-code driver-education item; and no other referral-producing clause is engaged.

Figures used: cancellation fee 4.50 SGD (EV-FARE-02717 / platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd); free waiting period 180 s (EV-TRIP-02717); measured continuous dwell 179 s (EV-GPS-02717).

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not; POL-NS-06 displaces the charge, so the 3.60 SGD payout the driver asks for is not earned. His anti-farming position (no_show_terminations_30d 2, a rate of 0.022 against 91 completed trips in 30 days) is accepted but never reached, because the fee itself was not earned.

CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. The evidence is clean: the GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (100 percent coverage, 74 fixes, maximum gap 0.0 s, both tracks present), the chat log reconciles to chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles to the fee in force — so no POL-NS-08 limb (a) to (d) fires, no artifact carrying the deciding fact is impaired below 1.0, and confidence (0.90) sits above the 0.70 floor. This is not a POL-NS-09 escalation. The monetary effect (4.50 SGD) is below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund executes automatically on issue.

REFERRALS. None. The arrival marker was true, so no POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival record arises; the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one POL-NS-01 limb (d) expressly recognises, so there is no mis-selected-code driver-education item; and no other referral-producing clause is engaged.

Figures used: cancellation fee 4.50 SGD (EV-FARE-02717 / platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd); free waiting period 180 s (EV-TRIP-02717); measured continuous dwell 179 s (EV-GPS-02717)."},"discarded_claims":[]}

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable.

What the record shows. The driver accepted the trip at 22:30:19, drove to the pickup, and tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:38:37 while stationary 0.31 m from the pin. EV-GPS-02717 places 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the arrival test in POL-NS-02 is met and the marker is genuine; POL-NS-05 does not fire and the waiting clock is not recomputed. The driver's account is broadly borne out by the event chain — he was en route about 8.3 minutes and waited about three minutes — so the rider's description of an 'almost immediate' cancellation is not supported by the telemetry. That does not, however, decide the fee.

Why the fee cannot stand. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, which for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, the figure POL-NS-01(c) directs be read from the record). The platform's own trace measures the driver's single in-geofence run at 179 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 22:38:37 to termination at 22:41:36; 180 seconds from 22:38:37 elapsed at 22:41:37, so the trip was terminated one second early. Limb (c) fails on the dwell and limb (d) fails on the timing, and under POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present. The shortfall cannot be bridged: POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated traffic advisory of a qualifying type covers the pickup road, and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); in any event the trace shows only one in-geofence interval (run_count 1). POL-NS-06 is strict liability — the waiting period is the consideration the fee purchases — so the driver's submission that the one-second gap is a boundary effect of a 10-second export cadence does not displace the measured figure.

Driver compensation. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Here POL-NS-01 fails and POL-NS-06 displaces the charge, so no payout arises. The anti-farming check is not reached; had it been, the driver's profile (no_show_terminations_30d 2, completed_trips_30d 91, rate 0.022) would not have tripped it, and no other profile field bears on the case. The rider's own POL-NS-04 submission — that the rider sent nothing and her track sat 895–903 m from the pin — is accepted but moot, since POL-NS-04 is not needed to reach this outcome.

Amount, evidence and execution. The refunded figure is the cancellation-fee line on the ledger: EV-FARE-02717 shows cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The full contested amount of $4.50 is returned. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts, EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, are both COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, and the fee line reconciles with platform_policy, so POL-NS-08(d) has nothing to bite on, nothing caps confidence below the 0.70 floor and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is presented. No clause requires a referral. The monetary effect ($4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold ($8.00), so this ruling is executed automatically.

Both parties: this case is decided by the driver's own GPS export and trip record, and they agree with each other. The driver genuinely arrived and his arrival marker was honest: EV-GPS-02717 shows 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, the closest 0.31 m from the pin, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied and POL-NS-05 does not fire (at the 22:38:37 'I'm Here' tap he was stationary essentially on the pin, far inside both the 50 m radius and the 300 m false-marker leash). The charge nevertheless fails on the waiting clock. POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, which is 180 seconds read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02717). That dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 22:38:37, not from the arrival tap and not from the wait-timer event. EV-GPS-02717 measures the run at 179.0 seconds (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec), a shortfall of 1.0 second. The driver terminated the trip at 22:41:36, one second before the required dwell elapsed at 22:41:37, so limb (d)'s timing requirement also fails: it is true, as the driver says, that RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three reason codes limb (d) recognises and that no boarding event is recorded, but limb (d) additionally requires termination at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and it was not. The driver's 'boundary effect' argument is rejected: no clause gives a de minimis tolerance on the waiting period, and POL-NS-06 is deliberately strict, so the 1-second shortfall on his own admissible trace is decisive. Bridging under POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable in any event, because run_count is 1 (there is no second in-geofence interval to sum) and EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, which makes limb (i) unavailable rather than exculpatory. The rider's account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the telemetry (accepted 22:30:19, 8.3 minutes en route, cancellation 22:41:36), and the rider sent no message during the waiting window so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider; neither point changes the outcome, because POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responsive. On the money: the fare_breakdown line is the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 with total_charged SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd SGD 0.00 (EV-FARE-02717), and it reconciles exactly to the SGD 4.50 in force, so POL-NS-08(d) has nothing to bite on and there is no integrity defect. The deciding facts are carried by EV-GPS-02717 and EV-TRIP-02717, both COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes (100% coverage, 10-second cadence, 0.0 s maximum gap), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires. POL-NS-07 pays the driver nothing here, because it pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-06 displaces it; the anti-farming check would not have barred a payout (no_show_terminations_30d 2 is below 4, and 2/91 = 0.022 is below 0.08), but that is moot. Result: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider under POL-NS-06 with no driver compensation; the monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. Both parties may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The driver's own trace measures the continuous in-geofence dwell at 179 seconds — a single run of 19 consecutive fixes from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36 — against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180, which is the figure POL-NS-01(c) directs be read from the record rather than from fee_schedule.defaults). POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous dwell of at least that free waiting period. 179 seconds does not meet 180, so limb (c) fails by one second. POL-NS-06 then governs: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

Independently of limb (c), limb (d) of POL-NS-01 also fails. For limb (d) the trip must be terminated at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and the dwell runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix — 22:38:37 — not from the driver's arrival tap. 180 seconds from 22:38:37 elapses at 22:41:37, but the trip was terminated at 22:41:36, one second early. The driver's own statement that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is therefore contradicted by his own trace, which records a 1-second shortfall. Because limbs (c) and (d) both fail, the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the refund falls to be made under POL-NS-06.

The driver cannot bridge the one-second gap by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, with geometry covering the pickup road and an active window covering the waiting period, carries a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING — the artifact carries no payload and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own record states that no advisory covers Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 in this window. A MISSING advisory makes limb (i) unavailable, so it cannot be asserted to excuse or extend the shortfall. In any event the trace shows only a single in-geofence interval (accumulated_dwell.run_count = 1), so there is no second interval for limb (i) to add to the first. The 179-second shortfall therefore stands unmodified.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it'. Here POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full — limbs (c) and (d) each fail on the 179-second dwell — and POL-NS-06 positively displaces the charge. The driver therefore has no payout under POL-NS-07, and the $4.50 cancellation fee is not a sum that has been earned and retained by him; it is a charge that should never have been levied.

The amount the rider contests is exactly the cancellation-fee line on the ledger: the fare_breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the rider filed this dispute. Refunding that line in full under POL-NS-06 returns the whole contested amount to the filing party, which is FULL_REFUND as POL-GEN-03 defines it. The rider's claim is that the $4.50 should not have been charged at all, and on the 179-second dwell that claim is entirely right.

The evidence carrying the deciding fact is clean and unimpaired, so the confidence cap on the governing artifacts does not fall below the platform-wide escalation floor and no escalation is required. Both the gps_trace (EV-GPS-02717) and the trip_record (EV-TRIP-02717) are rated COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes: 100.0% coverage, 10-second cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and 19 qualifying in-geofence fixes across the measured run, all well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (min_distance_m 0.31 m). The arrival marker at 22:38:37 is not a false marker — the first qualifying in-geofence fix falls at the same timestamp — so POL-NS-05 does not fire and nothing in the record casts doubt on the 179-second measurement. The shortfall is arithmetic on admissible evidence and the rider is entitled to a monetary ruling rather than a referral.

The driver's own trace proves arrival under POL-NS-02: 19 consecutive accuracy-qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, running continuously from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36, with his closest fix 0.31 m from the pickup pin. POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied on the platform's own measurement, not on the driver's say-so.

The arrival marker was true, so POL-NS-05 does not fire and the waiting clock is not recomputed: at the 22:38:37 'I'm Here' tap the trace places the driver stationary at 0.0 km/h essentially on the pin (0.31 m), far inside both the 50 m arrival radius and the 300 m POL-NS-05 leash. There is no false-arrival finding to make against him.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on its face: the trip was terminated by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises, and no boarding event is recorded anywhere in the trip record.

The fee line carries no integrity defect: the fare ledger's cancellation_fee of 4.50 SGD reconciles exactly with the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50 in force for this trip, so POL-NS-08(d) has nothing to bite on and there is no basis in the record to disturb the amount charged.

The evidence is clean and this case is decidable: the GPS export is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 100% coverage, 74 fixes, a maximum sampling gap of 0.0 s and both driver and rider tracks present, and the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count, so no limb of POL-NS-08 fires, nothing caps confidence below the floor and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is presented by this record.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from the rider during the waiting window, and the chat log contains exactly one message in total, sent by the driver ('im at the pickup point', 22:38:57, read 22:39:27). The rider sent nothing at all.

On the rider's own device track the rider never approached the pickup: 53 rider fixes all sit between 895 m and 903 m from the pin, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed and not merely undecidable.

The rider's account that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the platform's own telemetry: accepted 22:30:19, navigating from 22:30:27, arrival tapped 22:38:37 after 8.3 minutes en route, cancellation at 22:41:36 — the counterparty statement ('I waited the free period then cancelled') is what the event chain actually shows.

Nothing in the driver's profile bars compensation under POL-NS-07: no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4-termination limb, and against completed_trips_30d of 91 that is a rate of 0.022, below the 0.08 limb. Both limbs of the anti-farming check are required and neither trips; no other profile field may be read into that test.

On a fee that stands under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force — the money block computes 3.60 SGD against the 4.50 SGD fee — and the emitted outcome is a driver payment, not a bare declination.

The in-geofence dwell measured by the export is 179 seconds, one second short of the 180-second free waiting period, and the driver does not dispute that figure; but at every fix from 22:38:37 to 22:41:36 the driver was stationary on the pin and his trace runs on to 22:42:46 without him leaving, so the single-second difference is a boundary effect of a 10-second-cadence export rather than an early abandonment. There is in any event no second in-geofence interval for POL-NS-06(i) to add (run_count 1), and advisory EV-ADVIS-02717-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the driver's case does not rest on that limb.

The contested amount is the cancellation fee actually charged and still standing — payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, total_charged 4.50 — so on this rider-filed dispute a NO_ACTION outcome preserves the present payment state and the driver keeps the fee, unless some clause affirmatively displaces POL-NS-01.
